messages:
sam: CI alert: linux-gpu-kernels job failed on master after PR #2345 merge, looks like FlashAttention build errors + perf regression. attaching log snippet:

ci-bot: linux-gpu-kernels failed for commit d4c9a7e

sam: log:
```
In file included from flash_attn/cuda_kernels.cu:10:
flash_attn/kernel.cuh(234): error: identifier "wmma::load_matrix_sync" is undefined
error: ptxas fatal   : Unresolved function '_ZN4cutl9somethingEv'
```

maria: ugh. repro'd locally on my workstation (A100, Ubuntu20.04) after pulling master. latency on short chatbot requests jumped ~15-20% in our microbench.

jordan: is this only on flashattn_v2 or also fused kernels?

li: I ran the microbench across kernels this morning. quick numbers (median latency ms, seq=1024, batch=1):
- flash_attn_v1: 48ms
- flash_attn_v2: 62ms (bad)
- fused_attention: 51ms
- paged_attention: 55ms
so v2 regressed. build itself failed in CI though - looks like compilation errors on some toolchains.

anika: could be container/toolchain mismatch. CI image uses `nvidia/cuda:12.2-devel-ubuntu22.04` and our local dev image was 12.1 w/ gcc-12. different nvcc/PTX and CUDA toolkit headers can expose missing wmma symbols.

devon: I reproduced both the compile error and the perf delta in a clean docker from CI image. steps:
```
docker run --gpus all -it --rm nvidia/cuda:12.2-devel-ubuntu22.04 bash
apt update && apt install -y build-essential cmake python3 python3-pip gcc-11 g++-11
python3 -m pip install -r requirements.txt
cmake .. -DUSE_FLASHATTN=ON -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=gcc-11 -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=g++-11
make -j
```
compile fails as in CI. switching to gcc-11 fixes the build but results differ from our mac devkits.

maria: interesting. so toolchain mismatch between PR author and CI. PR changed a kernel wrapper around wmma and enabled ptx inline. that is fragile across nvcc versions.

jordan: short-term: pin gcc in CI image or add matrix entry. long-term: add configure guards to avoid using unsupported wmma calls when not available.

li: i bisected, looks like commit 9f2a1b toggled `USE_WMMA=ON` by default for sm80+. On CUDA12.2+ with nvcc 12.2 and gcc12 there are name mangling differences causing unresolved symbols.

anika: my proposal: 1) update CI Dockerfile to install gcc-11 and set as default for the kernel build stage; 2) add gcc-12 run to matrix to catch API differences; 3) revert enabling USE_WMMA by default until we add compatibility checks.

devon: i ran perf after pinning gcc-11 in the container and also tried setting compile flags: `-O3 -fPIC -march=skylake-avx512 -DNO_PTX_INLINE` and that gives baseline latency back: flash_attn_v2 -> 49ms.

sam: can you paste the minimal cmake flags we should use in CI?

devon: yes: `cmake .. -DUSE_FLASHATTN=ON -DUSE_WMMA=ON -DCUDA_TOOLKIT_ROOT_DIR=/usr/local/cuda -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=/usr/bin/gcc-11 -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=/usr/bin/g++-11 -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release`

maria: also saw a KV-cache interaction: under high-concurrency (batching enabled) the v2 kernel spilled extra memory causing eviction more often. profiling trace shows extra memcpy and sync points. stack from perf: `kernel_launch -> kv_cache_serialize -> memcpyAsync -> cudaDeviceSynchronize` which shouldn't be there.

li: that memcpy/sync came from our fallback code path when `WMMA` not present; it serializes kv cache to keep memory layout consistent. when compiled with incompatible toolchain some inlined path triggers fallback at runtime.

anika: action items:
- anika: open PR to update dockerfile + pin gcc-11 for kernel builds and add gcc-12 job (WIP).
- devon: prepare a tiny repro script and perf numbers to include in the PR.
- li: add a runtime feature check for WMMA and guard the default enabling.
- jordan: add a CI test that runs small attention perf on a smoke matrix.

ops-bot: created issue RW-INC-432: "FlashAttention v2: CI compile errors & perf regressions" and assigned to eng-runtime.

anika: PR opened: #2387 - changes Dockerfile, pins gcc-11, adds gcc-12 job. plz review.

sam: reviewed quickly. two nits. can we also add a short note in dev docs about how to reproduce the kernel build (which docker image to use, gcc versions)?

devon: added `perf/repro_flashattn.py` and CI job runs it on a smaller config (seq=512,batch=1) to catch regressions. sample run: `python perf/repro_flashattn.py --kernel flash_attn_v2 --iters 50` outputs baseline numbers and a small CSV.

maria: after PR merged into staging and forcing gcc-11 in CI, the linux-gpu-kernels job now passes. benchmark after merge on same hardware: flash_attn_v2 median 50ms. regression mitigated.

jordan: follow-up: we still should make kernels robust across toolchains. opening follow-up RFC to discuss compile guards, feature detection, and tweaking PTX inline choices.

sam: thanks all. labeling RW-INC-432 resolved for now. leaving open for the RFC. :thumbsup:
